Kediri was a Hindu kingdom in east Java, on the Brantas river, from 1042 to 1222, with its capital at Daha. It was one of the two halves into which Airlangga split his realm (East Javanese kingdoms). It was the richer half and a centre of Old Javanese poetry: the Kakawin Bharatayuddha, a retelling of the war in the Mahabharata, was written there in 1157.

In 1222 Ken Arok overthrew its king and founded Singhasari. The map shows Kediri from 1279 to 1400, when Daha rose again. In 1292 Jayakatwang of Kediri killed the last king of Singhasari. The next year a Mongol fleet landed, and Raden Wijaya used it to defeat Jayakatwang before turning on the Mongols. He then founded Majapahit, and Daha became one of its royal seats.
